description: Recommends Council reaffirm city's leadership in homelessness plan.
Endorses performance indicators for monitoring plan progress.
Future budget requests for the plan will be brought forward separately.

chips.text: Karen Kobussen stated previous homelessness plans have not produced measurable results.
Saskatoon Crisis Intervention Service supports 80 high-complexity individuals.
Administration clarified the city is not endorsing parts of the plan outside its jurisdiction.
The exact number of people on waiting lists for high-acuity homelessness services is unknown.
Multiple delegates supported the plan, emphasizing collaboration and diverse housing options.
The plan emphasizes Indigenous leadership and culturally appropriate responses.

speakers.name: Karen Kobussen
speakers.summary: Karen Kobussen, Saskatoon West Business Association, expressed concerns with the effectiveness of existing approaches to addressing homelessness and encouraged consideration of alternative strategies, enhanced performance measurement, an...
said: Current plan is "history repeated," hasn't produced measurable results.
More funding led to more homelessness; money serves, not solves.
Need smarter money, quality by-name data, focus on prevention/diversion.

speakers.name: Rob Wilgenhof
speakers.summary: Rob Wilgenhof expressed support for the City's efforts to address homelessness and addictions and encouraged consideration of additional community-based response measures to complement existing emergency services.
said: Asks if an immediate triage response team is being developed.
Such a team could reduce strain on emergency services.

speakers.name: Mathieu Gaudet
speakers.summary: Mathieu Gaudet, Métis Nation–Saskatchewan, expressed support of the Plan highlighting the collaborative development of the plan, emphasized the importance of coordinated efforts among partners, and encouraged continued support for implem...
said: Endorses the plan, a community-driven roadmap for collaboration.
Highlights three priorities and Indigenous leadership.
M&S is already aligning investments with the plan.

speakers.name: Gordon Taylor
speakers.summary: Gordon Taylor, Executive Director, The Salvation Army, expressed support for the Plan and highlighted the importance of a range of housing and shelter options, as well as continued investment in services and supports to assist individual...
said: Emphasizes transitional/supportive housing and operational funding.
Advocates for basic shelters over undignified warming centers.
Warns against clustering large overnight locations in one neighborhood.

speakers.name: Colleen Christopherson-Cote
speakers.summary: Colleen Christopherson-Cote, Saskatoon Poverty Reduction Partnership, spoke in support of the Plan emphasizing the importance of a coordinated, community-wide approach to addressing homelessness and poverty and highlighted the need for c...
said: Plan is a shared roadmap, requires collective accountability.
Housing alone is not the solution; income inequality is critical.
City's role includes policy, land use, and bold advocacy.

speakers.name: Jodie Semkiw
speakers.organization: Executive Director, Saskatoon Crisis Intervention Service
speakers.summary: Jodie Semkiw, Executive Director, Saskatoon Crisis Intervention Service, spoke in support of the Plan highlighting the importance of housing stability, coordinated community services, and ongoing supports for individuals with complex nee...
said: Supports plan, emphasizing housing first and wrap-around supports.
Their program serves high-acuity individuals with complex needs.
Focus on coordinated systems, prevention, reconciliation, and dignity.

speakers.name: Robert Lafontaine
speakers.summary: Robert Lafontaine, Saskatoon Housing Initiatives Partnership, was in the gallery and was called forward to respond to questions of Committee regarding homelessness data collection, reporting practices, and ongoing efforts to improve data...
said: HYFAS tracks inflows/outflows for Reaching Home projects.
Working to expand data sharing and release information publicly.
Estimates 30% of homelessness data might be missing.

description: Council members provided updates on their activities.
